description: Patch detection: tickets.update_fields renders the new patch UX; tickets.create (no patch object) renders the legacy form unchanged
Target framing shows the reference source ('the ticket from <step name>') when ticket_id is mapped by reference, and updates when switched to fixed/expression
Adding a Status change from the dialog's field catalog and picking a status emits patch: { status_id } only; other keys absent; catalog marks Status as added
Collapsed step shows summary-first presentation with 'Edit changes…' opening the dialog; dialog reuses mapping-field components (dependent picker works inside it)
Removing a change row removes the key from the emitted definition JSON
Round-trip: a definition with patch {status_id, priority_id, due_date: null} loads showing exactly those three changes (due date as 'Clear value') and re-saves byte-identical
patch.assignment renders as one change entry; dependent pickers (assignment primary type → user picker) still resolve
Change summary in panel and on step card reflects configured changes with display labels and '+N more' capping
Advanced section: expected_updated_at, idempotency_key, custom_fields, attributes, Raw JSON are collapsed by default and functional when expanded
Raw JSON round-trip: entering valid JSON in Advanced then switching to structured shows the fields as change rows; invalid JSON shows translated inline error
Empty patch shows 'Add at least one field to change' guidance and blocks publish via existing validation, with the friendly message on the badge
Playwright: author a tickets.update_fields step end-to-end via the new UX, publish, run against seeded data; only the configured fields change on the ticket (DB-verified)
Contacts/clients/projects/opportunities update actions each render the new UX from schema alone (snapshot/smoke, no per-action code)
New interactive elements expose stable ids consumed by ui-reflection (spot-check via existing reflection test helpers)
